genes/0.notes: BBSOAS is caused by heterozygous NR2F1 sequence variants or deletions. Whole-gene deletion and many truncating or loss-of-function alleles produce haploinsufficiency. DNA-binding-domain missense variants can exert an additional dominant-negative effect and are associated with more severe neurodevelopmental manifestations, but genotype-phenotype correlations remain preliminary and should not be treated as deterministic. Residue 110 lies within the DBD: the p.Phe110del indel at the same residue is characterized as a within-DBD variant, and only p.Ala155Thr has been described as falling outside it. The de novo p.Phe110Leu missense variant reported in early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy is therefore a DBD allele, consistent with the severity correlation above rather than an exception to it.

evidence.snippet: There is no cure for NR2F1-NDD. Supportive treatment typically relies on multidisciplinary specialists in the fields of neurology, speech-language pathology, ophthalmology (including low-vision services), gastroenterology, nutrition, occupational therapy, physical therapy, audiology, clinical genetics, and genetic counseling.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies multidisciplinary supportive care as the management approach.

treatments/0.description: There is no cure for BBSOAS. Supportive management relies on multidisciplinary specialists including neurology, speech-language pathology, ophthalmology with low-vision services, gastroenterology, nutrition, occupational therapy, physical therapy, audiology, clinical genetics, and genetic counseling, with regular surveillance for existing and emerging manifestations.

evidence.snippet: Referral to an early intervention program is recommended for access to occupational, physical, speech, and feeding therapy as well as infant mental health services, special educators, and sensory impairment specialists.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends coordinated early developmental intervention.

treatments/1.description: Early intervention and individualized educational support should include physical, occupational, speech-language, feeding, and sensory-impairment services as indicated. Augmentative and alternative communication should be assessed when expressive language is limited.

evidence.snippet: Treatment of refractive errors
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends refractive, strabismus, and low-vision management.

evidence.snippet: Visual therapy focused on CVI
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends visual therapy and early intervention for CVI.

treatments/2.description: Ophthalmologic care should correct refractive errors or strabismus when present and provide low-vision services. Cerebral visual impairment may benefit from visual therapy and early intervention aimed at visual development; these measures are supportive rather than disease modifying.

evidence.snippet: Gastrostomy tube placement may be required for persistent feeding issues.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies feeding therapy and escalation for persistent problems.

treatments/3.description: Feeding-team and nutrition assessment should address poor suck, chewing or swallowing difficulty, growth, aspiration risk, and oral safety. Feeding therapy is used first; persistent dysphagia or unsafe intake may require enteral support.

evidence.snippet: Standardized treatment w/ASM by experienced neurologist
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends standard neurologist-directed antiseizure treatment.

evidence.snippet: However, seizures were controlled in only 50% of previously reported cases, while all of the six new cases became seizure-free after perampanel as an add-on treatment.
evidence.explanation: A six-case observational series reports seizure freedom after add-on perampanel, supporting a hypothesis-generating treatment signal but not disorder-specific comparative superiority.

treatments/4.description: Epilepsy should be treated with individualized antiseizure pharmacotherapy under an experienced neurologist. A small observational NR2F1-related epilepsy series reported seizure freedom after add-on perampanel, but this signal does not establish comparative superiority or a standard regimen.

evidence.snippet: Regular monitoring of existing manifestations, the individual's response to supportive care, and the emergence of new manifestations.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews provides the overarching surveillance principle.

treatments/5.description: Follow-up should monitor growth and feeding safety, development and educational needs, seizures and new neurologic manifestations, behavior, mobility and self-help skills, visual function and low-vision needs, hearing, and family support needs at clinically appropriate intervals.

evidence.snippet: Given this risk, prenatal and preimplantation genetic testing may be considered.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends genetic counseling and testing options for recurrence risk.

treatments/6.description: Genetic counseling is recommended given the autosomal dominant inheritance and recurrence risk considerations, including the option of prenatal and preimplantation genetic testing.

evidence.snippet: Preliminary genotype-phenotype correlations based on published reports to date suggest
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews explicitly labels the genotype-phenotype correlation preliminary.

open_questions/0.rationale: Haploinsufficiency is established for deletions and many loss-of-function alleles. DNA-binding-domain variants may act dominant negatively and show a more severe cohort-level phenotype, but available series are small and the effect cannot be generalized to every missense or truncating allele.

evidence.snippet: "PrevalenceClass": "<1 / 1 000 000"
evidence.explanation: Orphadata supplies the lower class-only estimate.

evidence.snippet: estimated prevalence from 1:100,000 to 1:250,000 people worldwide
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews supplies the higher literature estimate.

open_questions/1.rationale: Orphadata provides a class-only estimate below one per million, whereas GeneReviews cites approximately one per 100,000 to one per 250,000. Underdiagnosis, different denominators, and reuse of early case counts may contribute, but no population-based study resolves the discrepancy.

evidence.snippet: for those individuals with available longitudinal ophthalmological data, there was no significant deterioration in visual function during the period of follow-up.
evidence.explanation: The cohort supports stability over observed follow-up, not the entire lifespan.

open_questions/2.rationale: Existing longitudinal observations favor a developmental, non-progressive optic neuropathy, but the cohort is small, follow-up is uneven, and adult data are sparse. The entry therefore describes the visual course as generally rather than universally non-progressive.

evidence.snippet: Our data point to an active role for NR2F1 in the mitochondrial gene expression regulatory network in neurons and support the involvement of mitochondrial dysfunction in BBSOAS pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: The publication frames mitochondrial involvement as supported by model data.

open_questions/3.rationale: The mouse data identify altered mitochondrial genes, proteins, mass, and morphology, but no human neural-tissue validation or clinical biomarker currently establishes this branch as a driver in affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: Both mutations cause mislocalization from the cell membrane to the cytosol, and structural modeling reveals that both mutations lie within a calcium-sensitive domain near the active site.
evidence.explanation: Shows mislocalization of the founding ADNIV mutants in transfected HEK293T cells, which the source interprets as suggesting the mutations may alter a membrane-binding property of the protein.

evidence.snippet: Capn5 knockout mice have no observable phenotype
evidence.explanation: Knockout-mouse evidence arguing against haploinsufficiency and supporting a gain-of-function mechanism for ADNIV.

evidence.snippet: Although these mutations could cause disease through haploinsufficiency, it seems more likely that they result in a gain of function of calpain-5 that causes harm to the photoreceptor cells.
evidence.explanation: The gene-discovery paper weighs haploinsufficiency against gain of function and favours gain of function, the category recorded here. Graded OTHER because the sentence is the authors' own reasoning in discussion rather than a reported clinical finding; the same sentence carries that grade on the entry's refuted_haploinsufficiency_model hypothesis.

steps/1.description: Heterozygous missense mutations near the calcium-sensitive gating loop of the calpain-5 catalytic core increase calcium sensitivity and catalytic activity of the enzyme; in transfected HEK293T cells the founding mutant proteins localize to the cytoplasm rather than near the cell surface, suggesting the mutations may alter a membrane-binding property of calpain-5. The regulatory domain-III variant G376S has not been functionally assayed and is only hypothesized to have a milder effect on protein function. Capn5 knockout mice show no retinal phenotype, indicating the disease mechanism is gain-of-function rather than haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: we observed a significant fraction of proteins localized to the synapse in controls that decreased in CAPN5-NIV vitreous. Among these proteins were: neurexin-2 (NRXN2), glutamate receptor 4 (GluR4), neurofascin (NFASC)
evidence.explanation: Vitreous proteomics documents decreased synaptic proteins in CAPN5-NIV patients, consistent with aberrant calpain-mediated synaptic proteolysis, though the study could not attribute the losses to a specific retinal cell type.

evidence.snippet: However, our proteomic analysis could not differentiate which retinal cells are affected by loss of these proteins in CAPN5-NIV
evidence.explanation: Explicit caveat from the same proteomic study: the retinal cell type(s) losing these synaptic proteins could not be determined, so a photoreceptor-specific attribution is not established. Recorded as NO_EVIDENCE because the sentence carries no evidence bearing on whether the proteolysis is photoreceptor-specific; it bounds the node's photoreceptor cell-type binding rather than asserting the node's proteolysis claim.

evidence.snippet: Electroretinography showed mutant mouse eyes had a selective loss of the b-wave indicating an inner-retina signaling defect.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model evidence linking mutant CAPN5 expression to the reduced ERG b-wave, the earliest clinical/electrophysiological correlate of synaptic dysfunction.

steps/2.description: Hyperactive, mislocalized calpain-5 is hypothesized to aberrantly proteolyze substrates at the retinal ribbon synapse in the retina's naturally high-calcium phototransduction environment; the specific protein substrates of calpain-5 have not been identified. Vitreous proteomics of CAPN5-NIV patients shows early loss of synaptic proteins including neurexin-2, glutamate receptor 4 (a receptor expressed in rod bipolar cells), and neurofascin. The proteomic analysis could not differentiate which retinal cells are affected by these losses, which may contribute to the synaptic signaling defect -- reduced ERG b-wave amplitude -- seen in early disease.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of gene expression changes in the hCAPN5(R243L) mouse retina showed upregulation of several markers, including members of the Toll-like receptor pathway, chemokines and cytokines, indicative of both an innate and adaptive immune response.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model transcriptomic evidence for innate and adaptive immune pathway activation downstream of mutant CAPN5 expression.

evidence.snippet: Chronic inflammatory CD3-positive cell infiltrates were identified throughout the uvea, vitreous and retina, consistent with chronic uveitis.
evidence.explanation: Human histopathology directly demonstrating CD3+ T-cell infiltration of the uvea, vitreous, and retina in an enucleated ADNIV eye.

evidence.snippet: This analysis showed that TNF-α levels were normal, explaining why infliximab therapy failed in these patients
evidence.explanation: Documents normal vitreous TNF-alpha in CAPN5-NIV patient samples, supporting the node's claim that anti-TNF immunosuppression (infliximab) fails in these patients.

steps/3.description: Aberrant proteolysis and the resulting cellular stress may trigger local innate immune activation (Toll-like receptor pathway genes, chemokines, cytokines, complement components) accompanied by dense CD3+ T-lymphocyte infiltration of the uvea, vitreous, and retina, driving chronic autoimmune uveitis; how the innate and adaptive arms interact in CAPN5-NIV pathogenesis remains under investigation. Vitreous TNF-alpha levels are normal, explaining why patients fail conventional anti-TNF immunosuppression (e.g. infliximab).

evidence.snippet: There were proteins with known antioxidant activity present in controls that were absent in CAPN5-NIV vitreous: superoxide dismutase (SOD1 and SOD3), peroxiredoxin (PRDX2 and PRDX6), catalase (CAT), clusterin, and glutathione peroxidase 3 (GPX3).
evidence.explanation: Vitreous proteomics documents loss of multiple antioxidant defense proteins, supporting oxidative stress as a driver of photoreceptor degeneration.

steps/4.description: Chronic inflammation is accompanied by loss of vitreous antioxidant defenses (superoxide dismutase, peroxiredoxins, catalase, clusterin), indicating reduced defense against oxidative stress that may leave photoreceptors vulnerable to oxidative injury. A retinitis-pigmentosa-like pigmentary photoreceptor degeneration (ADNIV Stage II) follows, distinguished from classic RP by pigment clumping rather than bone-spicule pigmentation.

evidence.snippet: Among the significantly-downregulated proteins were several proteins involved in retinal function: retinoschisin (RS1), and opticin (OPTC)
evidence.explanation: Documents opticin among the significantly downregulated proteins in CAPN5-NIV vitreous; the paper proposes that opticin downregulation may contribute to the increased retinal neovascularization seen in these patients.

evidence.snippet: It was further revealed that the CAPN5-NIV vitreous contained abundant levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), T-cell proliferative markers, and interleukin-6 (IL-6).
evidence.explanation: Documents elevated vitreous VEGF as the angiogenic driver of CAPN5-NIV retinal/iris neovascularization.

steps/5.description: Downregulation of the anti-angiogenic vitreous matrix protein opticin may contribute, together with elevated vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), to pathologic retinal and iris neovascularization mimicking proliferative diabetic retinopathy (ADNIV Stage III). Anti-VEGF therapy (bevacizumab) has been repositioned to suppress this neovascularization.

evidence.snippet: Among the downregulated pro-teins was versican (VCAN/CSPG2). Versican is a chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan involved in maintaining the physiologic structure of the vitreous.
evidence.explanation: Documents versican among the downregulated proteins in CAPN5-NIV vitreous and its role in maintaining vitreous structure. (The quoted text preserves the source PDF's line-break hyphenation in "pro-teins".)

evidence.snippet: The eye showed exudative retinal detachment and neovascularization, intraocular fibrosis, and features of phthisis bulbi.
evidence.explanation: Human histopathology of a Stage V ADNIV eye documenting the terminal fibrotic/phthisical outcome.

steps/6.description: Downregulation of the vitreous structural proteoglycan versican may disrupt normal vitreous architecture, contributing to intraocular fibrosis, epiretinal membrane formation, and tractional retinal detachment (ADNIV Stage IV). Structural damage is generally irreversible; the disease culminates in phthisis bulbi and complete blindness (Stage V) despite corticosteroid control of active inflammation.

evidence.snippet: CAPN5 encodes calpain-5, a calcium-activated cysteine protease that is expressed in retinal photoreceptor cells. Both mutations cause mislocalization from the cell membrane to the cytosol, and structural modeling reveals that both mutations lie within a calcium-sensitive domain near the active site.
evidence.explanation: Establishes CAPN5 as the causal gene. The mislocalization was demonstrated in transfected HEK293T cells (with structural modeling of the calcium-sensitive domain), not in patient photoreceptors.

evidence.snippet: Two daughters of an affected mother demonstrated symptoms of stage III ADNIV, with posterior uveitis, cystoid macular edema, intraocular fibrosis, retinal neovascularization, retinal degeneration, and cataract. The women also harbored a novel guanine to thymine (c.750G>T, p.Lys250Asn) missense mutation in exon 6 of CAPN5
evidence.explanation: Documents the K250N (c.750G>T) gating-loop variant and its severe uveitic/neovascular phenotype in an affected kindred.

evidence.snippet: Next-generation sequencing identified that the patient was heterozygous for CAPN5 c.799G>A, p.(Gly267Ser).
evidence.explanation: Documents the severe catalytic-domain G267S variant and its genotype-phenotype correlation with disease severity.

evidence.snippet: The CAPN5 variant c.1126G>A, p.(Gly376Ser) was identified in this patient. This variant is present at an allele frequency of 0.017% in the South Asian population within the Exome Aggregate Consortium (ExAC) database13.
evidence.explanation: Documents the mild regulatory-domain G376S variant, the first reported outside the catalytic domain.

genes/0.notes: Encodes calpain-5, a 640-amino-acid calcium-activated cysteine protease expressed in retinal photoreceptor cells. All known pathogenic variants are heterozygous, germline, and missense -- clustering either in the catalytic protease core near the calcium-sensitive gating loop (R243L, L244P, K250N, G267S, R289W) or in regulatory domain-III (G376S); the functionally tested variants are gain-of-function. Capn5 knockout mice show no retinal phenotype, arguing against haploinsufficiency as the disease mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in CAPN5 trigger autoimmune uveitis characterized by inflammatory T-cells and severe neovascularization.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the T-cell-mediated autoimmune uveitis that corticosteroid therapy targets.

evidence.snippet: This is supported by studies which found that intraocular steroids suppress inflammatory cells and neovascularisation but not retinal fibrosis or degeneration in ADNIV patients
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the incomplete steroid response: inflammation and neovascularization are suppressed but the fibrotic/degenerative component is not.

treatments/0.description: Corticosteroids are used to control active intraocular inflammation; intraocular steroids suppress inflammatory cells and neovascularization but not the retinal fibrosis or degenerative component of disease.

evidence.snippet: Based on this, we repositioned bevacizumab (anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody), intravitreal methotrexate (T-cell inhibi-tor), and tocilizumab (anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody) and successfully mitigated neovascularization, inflamma-tory cell infiltration, and persistent fibrosis in these patients
evidence.explanation: Documents the proteomics-guided repositioning of bevacizumab and its successful mitigation of neovascularization in CAPN5-NIV patients. (The quoted text preserves the source PDF's line-break hyphenation in "inhibi-tor" and "inflamma-tory".)

treatments/1.description: Intravitreal bevacizumab, an anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, was repositioned based on proteomic evidence of elevated vitreous VEGF and successfully mitigated neovascularization in CAPN5-NIV patients.

evidence.snippet: He had multiple cryotherapy treatments, left eye ruthenium plaque brachytherapy and underwent bilateral pars plana vitrectomies.
evidence.explanation: Documents multiple cryotherapy treatments used to manage progressive vasoproliferative CAPN5-NIV disease.

treatments/2.description: Retinal cryotherapy has been used in CAPN5-NIV: a severely affected patient with progressive vitreoretinopathy and recurrent vitreous hemorrhages received multiple cryotherapy treatments. Disease-specific indication and outcome data are limited to single-case experience.

evidence.snippet: He had multiple cryotherapy treatments, left eye ruthenium plaque brachytherapy and underwent bilateral pars plana vitrectomies.
evidence.explanation: Documents left-eye ruthenium plaque brachytherapy used for advanced vasoproliferative CAPN5-NIV disease.

treatments/3.description: Ruthenium plaque brachytherapy has been used in CAPN5-NIV: a severely affected patient with progressive vitreoretinopathy and recurrent vitreous hemorrhages received left-eye plaque brachytherapy. Disease-specific indication and outcome data are limited to single-case experience.

evidence.snippet: He had multiple cryotherapy treatments, left eye ruthenium plaque brachytherapy and underwent bilateral pars plana vitrectomies.
evidence.explanation: Documents pars plana vitrectomy as part of the surgical management of advanced CAPN5-NIV.

treatments/4.description: Pars plana vitrectomy has been used in the surgical management of advanced CAPN5-NIV: a severely affected patient with progressive vitreoretinopathy, recurrent vitreous hemorrhages, and subsequent tractional retinal detachments underwent bilateral vitrectomies. Disease-specific indication and outcome data are limited to single-case experience.

evidence.snippet: these patients are left with few treatment options and fail conventional immunosuppressive therapy, such as oral corticosteroids and infliximab
evidence.explanation: Documents the treatment-resistance to conventional immunosuppression, including anti-TNF therapy (infliximab), that distinguishes CAPN5-NIV biology.

treatments/5.description: Systemic immunosuppression is used for substantial vascular leakage/inflammation, but CAPN5-NIV patients characteristically fail conventional agents including anti-TNF-alpha therapy (infliximab), consistent with normal vitreous TNF-alpha levels and a treatment-resistant biology distinct from classic autoimmune uveitis.

evidence.snippet: Capn5 knockout mice have no observable phenotype
evidence.explanation: Knockout mice lacking a phenotype argues against haploinsufficiency, supporting the gain-of-function model.

hypotheses/0.description: ADNIV-causing CAPN5 variants act through gain-of-function protease hyperactivation and mislocalization rather than loss of normal calpain-5 function. This is the predominant model, supported by Capn5 knockout mice lacking a retinal phenotype and by direct biochemical demonstration of increased calcium sensitivity and mislocalization in all tested disease variants.

evidence.snippet: Although these mutations could cause disease through haploinsufficiency, it seems more likely that they result in a gain of function of calpain-5 that causes harm to the photoreceptor cells.
evidence.explanation: The founding paper's own discussion weighs haploinsufficiency against gain of function and judges gain of function more likely; this is authors' reasoning rather than primary clinical data, and the paper does not definitively exclude a loss-of-function contribution.

evidence.snippet: In in vitro activity assays, the mutation increased calpain protease activity and made it far more active at low concentrations of calcium.
evidence.explanation: Direct biochemical demonstration that the R243L disease variant is catalytically hyperactive, not hypoactive, arguing against the haploinsufficiency model.

hypotheses/1.description: An initially plausible alternative hypothesis was that ADNIV variants act through simple loss of calpain-5 function (haploinsufficiency), analogous to CAPN3 loss-of-function causing limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The founding paper left the question open but judged gain of function more likely; the model is disfavored by the normal phenotype of Capn5-null mice and by subsequent in vitro data showing tested disease variants are catalytically hyperactive, not hypoactive.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that protein expression levels were low for all mutants, but some could be rescued by a lower temperature (30°C vs. 37°C) and/or the chemical chaperone glycerol.
evidence.explanation: The expression assay reports lower steady-state abundance and partial abundance rescue; enzymatic rescue is not established by this quote.

evidence.snippet: (NAD(P)H steroid dehydrogenase-like protein) encoding a 3beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase functioning in the cholesterol biosynthetic pathway
evidence.explanation: Identifies the enzymatic function that is lost.

steps/1.description: Pathogenic NSDHL variants impair the sterol dehydrogenase/decarboxylase component of the C4-demethylation complex. An expression study of thirteen disease-associated missense variants and one deletion found reduced protein abundance; temperature or glycerol partially increased abundance for some variants. These assays do not establish that all variants act through the same folding defect or that rescued protein has restored catalytic activity.

evidence.snippet: NSDHL is a 3beta-hydroxysterol dehydrogenase that is involved in the removal of C-4 methyl groups in one of the later steps of cholesterol biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: The primary mouse paper describes the established enzymatic function in its background.

evidence.snippet: CHILD syndrome results from loss of function mutations in the NSDHL gene, which leads to inhibition of cholesterol synthesis and accumulation of toxic metabolic intermediates in affected tissues.
evidence.explanation: The review describes reduced synthesis and precursor accumulation; these are separate consequences of the biosynthetic block.

steps/2.description: Impaired NSDHL activity limits removal of C4 methyl groups from sterol intermediates. Reduced downstream cholesterol supply and upstream precursor accumulation are distinct biochemical consequences.

evidence.snippet: CHILD syndrome results from loss of function mutations in the NSDHL gene, which leads to inhibition of cholesterol synthesis and accumulation of toxic metabolic intermediates in affected tissues.
evidence.explanation: The review describes reduced synthesis and precursor accumulation; these are separate consequences of the biosynthetic block.

evidence.snippet: Taken together, these results demonstrate that cholesterol depletion is sufficient to account for virtually all of the reduced response of mutant GCPs to SHH in vitro.
evidence.explanation: Cholesterol supplementation experiments locate a major SHH-response defect in the recipient granule-cell cultures.

steps/3.description: Cholesterol supply can be insufficient within affected cells despite near-normal circulating sterols. In conditional-null mouse granule-cell cultures, cholesterol or LDL supplementation restored much of the impaired SHH response. This does not imply uniform systemic hypocholesterolemia.

evidence.snippet: The concentration of methylsterols was significantly higher in NsdhlΔ5/Y GCPs than Nsdhlflx5/Y GCPs (P < 0.002) in all four culture conditions.
evidence.explanation: Cultured conditional-null mouse granule-cell precursors accumulate methylsterols under the tested conditions.

evidence.snippet: Ketoconazole treatment did not affect the viability of WT cells, but it significantly increased mutant cell viability (from 65 to 78%; Fig. 7B).
evidence.explanation: An upstream synthesis inhibitor improved viability in mutant cultures; this supports a precursor-associated injury component but does not identify every accumulated sterol as toxic.

evidence.snippet: Although the reduction of methylsterol levels by ketoconazole treatment apparently improved the viability and cell morphology of the mutant GCPs, it had no effect on Gli1 expression
evidence.explanation: Cell viability and SHH transcriptional responses were experimentally dissociable; lowering precursors alone did not restore this readout.

steps/4.description: C4-methylsterol intermediates accumulate upstream of the NSDHL block. Mouse granule-cell experiments associate precursor reduction with improved viability, but different sterol species and endpoints need separate interpretation. The same intervention did not restore SHH-induced Gli1 expression.

evidence.snippet: However, RT-PCR on cDNA from keratinocytes and fibroblasts isolated from the affected versus clinically unaffected side in Patient #1 demonstrated exclusive expression of the mutant allele by affected cultured keratinocytes, while unaffected keratinocytes solely expressed the wild type allele
evidence.explanation: Cultures from one patient showed side-specific NSDHL allele expression; this is not a longitudinal measure of cell clearance.

evidence.snippet: Only the normal allele was expressed by unaffected fibroblasts, but fibroblasts from the clinically affected area expressed an approximately even distribution of normal and mutant alleles.
evidence.explanation: Fibroblast expression in affected skin did not match the exclusively mutant keratinocyte pattern.

steps/5.description: X-inactivation creates functional mosaicism in heterozygous females. In one patient, cultured keratinocytes from affected and unaffected skin expressed different NSDHL alleles, while affected fibroblasts retained both. These observations do not explain the precise midline boundary or demonstrate longitudinal cell clearance.

evidence.snippet: These data suggest that the higher percentage of WT hepatocytes present in livers from older Bpa1H females is the cumulative result of postnatal differences in either the growth rate or survival of WT vs mutant hepatocytes.
evidence.explanation: Cross-sectional age groups support selection in mouse liver while leaving differential survival versus proliferation unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The average percentage of NSDHL positive hepatocytes in livers from six Bpa1H P6 females was 52 (SD: 5). Among six mutant livers at P25, the average percentage of NSDHL positive hepatocytes increased to 62 (SD: 9).
evidence.explanation: The comparison concerns different mouse age groups and liver tissue, not serial biopsies of human skin.

steps/6.description: Mouse liver and brain show an age-dependent reduction in the representation of NSDHL-deficient cells. This is tissue-specific: NSDHL-negative skin persisted at eight weeks. The mechanism may involve differential survival or proliferation, and the result has not been measured longitudinally in human CHILD skin.

evidence.snippet: Individual organelles displayed few internal lamellae, which often fused prematurely into intracellular, multivesicular bodies that were incompletely secreted
evidence.explanation: Pretreatment patient biopsies demonstrate abnormal lamellar-body architecture and incomplete secretion.

evidence.snippet: Electron microscopy revealed vesicular structures in the intercellular spaces of the stratum corneum and vacuoles or vesicular structures in upper prickle cell layer. Some of them can be recognized as abnormal lamellar granules. Within the foamy cells in the papillary dermis, large vacuoles were found.
evidence.explanation: Independent ultrastructural confirmation of the abnormal lamellar granules and of the dermal foam cells this description asserts, from a different patient and laboratory than the treatment study.

steps/7.description: Patient biopsies show lamellar bodies with few internal lamellae, premature fusion, and incomplete secretion. The resulting retention of organelle material is a cellular secretory defect distinct from the extracellular lipid architecture it produces.

evidence.snippet: We replicated the granule cell precursor proliferation defect in vitro and demonstrate that it results from defective signaling by SHH.
evidence.explanation: The experiment is in cultured mouse granule-cell precursors rather than whole animals or human limb tissue.

evidence.snippet: Using mice that express lacZ under the control of the Gli1 promoter, we were also able to demonstrate variable, but reduced, induction of this SHH response gene in vivo
evidence.explanation: A separate reporter experiment demonstrates reduced SHH response in the conditional mouse CNS.

evidence.snippet: Further, affected placentas from mutant Nsdhl(Bpa-8H) male embryos demonstrate markedly decreased or no Ptch1-lacZ staining and no migration of Ihh expressing cells into the developing placenta.
evidence.explanation: Placental reporter and cellular-distribution observations implicate Hedgehog signaling in this mouse allele.

evidence.snippet: Although the reduction of methylsterol levels by ketoconazole treatment apparently improved the viability and cell morphology of the mutant GCPs, it had no effect on Gli1 expression
evidence.explanation: Cell viability and SHH transcriptional responses were experimentally dissociable; lowering precursors alone did not restore this readout.

steps/8.description: Conditional Nsdhl-null mouse granule-cell cultures have an impaired response to SHH that is strongly improved by cholesterol supply. Reduced reporter activity is also observed in mouse cerebellum and placenta. These findings concern signal reception and response; defective ligand processing and the precise mechanisms of human limb defects are not established.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, depletion of either SC4MOL or NSDHL significantly reduced the amount of fluorescently labeled EGFR ... associated with RAB11-positive recycling endosomes after 30 minutes of EGF stimulation.
evidence.explanation: NSDHL knockdown in experimental cells reduced receptor localization to recycling endosomes; this is not a patient-tissue result.

evidence.snippet: Conversely, SC4MOL and NSDHL-deficient cells showed an accelerated concentration of internalized fluorescently labeled EGF in RAB7-positive ... or EGFR in LAMP1-positive late endosomes
evidence.explanation: Experimental depletion shifts receptor-associated signals toward late endosomal compartments.

steps/9.description: NSDHL depletion in experimental cell systems reduces EGFR recycling and shifts receptor-associated signals toward late endosomal and lysosomal compartments. The assays use knockdown and model cells, not direct measurements in human CHILD lesions.

evidence.snippet: The reduced intracellular EGFR staining was accompanied by a marked loss of phosphorylated (activated) Y1173-EGFR ... signal in the NSDHL-null areas.
evidence.explanation: NSDHL-null patches of mouse skin had reduced activated EGFR; the original sentence also reports reduced ERK and AKT phosphorylation.

evidence.snippet: The NSDHL-null areas of the skin also exhibited significantly reduced proliferation, as determined by Ki-67 ... expression and in vivo BrdU incorporation
evidence.explanation: Mouse skin proliferation was reduced, so human hyperkeratosis must not be generalized into a universal increase in cellular proliferation.

steps/10.description: NSDHL-null patches of mouse skin show reduced activated EGFR, ERK, and AKT signals with reduced proliferation and loricrin expression. These model observations suggest altered epidermal growth and differentiation, but do not demonstrate the same signaling state in patient skin.

evidence.snippet: Finally, and as a result of impaired secretion, the stratum corneum extracellular matrix displayed a paucity of secreted lamellar material, interspersed with abundant non-lamellar vesicles
evidence.explanation: The patient ultrastructure links impaired secretion to disorganized extracellular lipid lamellae.

evidence.snippet: Although no visible ichthyosiform features could be appreciated either clinically or by light microscopy, ultrastructural images displayed mild abnormalities in lamellar body internal contents and lamellar bilayer organization
evidence.explanation: Clinically unaffected skin from one patient had subtle structural abnormalities, so visible normality is not proof of a fully normal lipid barrier.

steps/11.description: The stratum corneum extracellular matrix in affected skin contains sparse lamellar material mixed with non-lamellar vesicles, consistent with a defective lipid barrier. Clinically unaffected skin can retain mild ultrastructural abnormalities.

evidence.snippet: Although no consistent anomalies were identified in affected male embryos themselves, the labyrinth layer of the fetal placenta was always thinner, with fewer fetal vessels and decreased proliferation of labyrinth trophoblast cells.
evidence.explanation: Several mouse alleles show a placental structural phenotype associated with prenatal lethality; it does not establish the cause of every male loss or a human placental lesion.

evidence.snippet: Further, affected placentas from mutant Nsdhl(Bpa-8H) male embryos demonstrate markedly decreased or no Ptch1-lacZ staining and no migration of Ihh expressing cells into the developing placenta.
evidence.explanation: Placental reporter and cellular-distribution observations implicate Hedgehog signaling in this mouse allele.

steps/12.description: Several Nsdhl mouse alleles show a thin placental labyrinth with reduced fetal vascularization and trophoblast proliferation. Embryonic death occurs at allele-dependent stages, including earlier death with Bpa1H. Placental abnormalities are associated with lethality in these models; the corresponding human mechanism remains unverified.

evidence.snippet: The mutant follicles were smaller and shorter than adjacent WT follicles and lacked hair shafts, consistent with defective anagen hair growth.
evidence.explanation: Mouse mutant skin shows defective postnatal anagen growth; initial P2 follicle morphology was not grossly abnormal.

evidence.snippet: By 6 months, treated skin largely normalized, but did not grow hair
evidence.explanation: Skin improvement and hair growth were distinct outcomes in two treated patients.

evidence.snippet: CHILD syndrome is characterized by unilateral distribution of ichthyosiform skin lesions and ipsilateral limb defects that range from shortening of the metacarpals and phalanges to absence of the entire limb.

evidence.snippet: Most of the skin lesions improve spontaneously, but some can cause lifelong morbidity. Lesions in the intertriginous areas tend to be more persistent; this is termed ptychotropism

steps/14.description: Inflammatory erythematous plaques with yellowish waxy scale usually appear at birth or in early infancy. Lesions can be patchy, follow Blaschko lines, or involve both sides. Many improve with age, while intertriginous lesions can persist and new lesions can arise later, including at sites of injury.

evidence.snippet: an inflammatory nevus with striking lateralization and strict midline demarcation, as well as ipsilateral hypoplasia of the body

evidence.explanation: The original delineation locates the demarcation anatomically, at the middle of the trunk.

evidence.snippet: A symmetric distribution of this nevus can exceptionally be seen in patients with CHILD syndrome, and this bilateral involvement should not mislead the clinician to any other diagnosis.

steps/15.description: Skin lesions typically have a sharp boundary at the body midline. Limited lesions can follow Blaschko lines, and molecularly confirmed bilateral, almost symmetric involvement has been reported; bilateral involvement does not exclude CHILD syndrome.

steps/16.description: Hemidysplasia, the H in the acronym: hypoplasia of one side of the body, involving skeletal structures and internal organs on the same side as the cutaneous eruption. evidence.snippet: SSCA and genomic sequence analysis of NSDHL identified in 6 patients with CHILD syndrome, including one boy as well as a mother and her daughter, mutations potentially impairing protein function.
evidence.explanation: Establishes NSDHL variants as the molecular cause in a patient series.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of CHILD syndrome is established in a female proband with a heterozygous NSDHL pathogenic variant identified by molecular genetic testing that results in loss of functional decarboxylating sterol-4-alpha-carboxylate 3-dehydrogenase, the protein encoded by NSDHL.

evidence.explanation: The original CK syndrome study demonstrates residual, temperature-sensitive function of its two studied alleles, supporting the distinction from severe CHILD loss of function.

evidence.snippet: The variant was confirmed by targeted Sanger sequencing for DNA from both skin tissues and blood. Testing of parental DNA indicated maternal inheritance, with her father testing negative for the variant.
evidence.explanation: The adult gastrointestinal case confirms maternal transmission of the reported NSDHL frameshift.

genes/0.notes: NSDHL loss-of-function variants cause CHILD syndrome. The Xq28 gene encodes the dehydrogenase/decarboxylase component of sterol C4-demethylation. Reported alleles include missense, premature termination, frameshift and exon-deletion variants. Familial transmission can occur with marked variability, including a mother with mild skin changes. Rare male survival can reflect postzygotic mosaicism. Hypomorphic variants retaining partial function cause the distinct allelic CK syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Topical treatment with lovastatin/cholesterol (but not cholesterol alone) virtually cleared skin lesions by 3 months, accompanied by histological and ultrastructural normalization of epidermal structure and lipid secretion.
evidence.explanation: Cholesterol alone did not improve the lesions in this two-patient sequence; there was no statin-only comparison to establish that the combination is required.

evidence.snippet: We report the case of a 10-year-old girl treated with topical simvastatin and cholesterol ointment, after which her skin lesions significantly improved within the first 30 days of treatment.
evidence.explanation: Independent case replication using simvastatin in place of lovastatin.

evidence.snippet: The authors report a 2-month-old patient presenting with typical features of CHILD syndrome that was treated with a topical solution containing cholesterol and lovastatin, with complete clearance of her CHILD nevus.
evidence.explanation: An additional infant case had clearance of the nevus with the combination.

evidence.snippet: Decreased inflammation, skin thickening, and scaling was noted as early as 4–6 weeks in both patients, and the severity scores decreased by 72% (patient 1) and 79% (patient 2) by 3 months.
evidence.explanation: The uncontrolled two-patient study reports separate within-patient severity-score reductions, not comparative efficacy.

evidence.snippet: We first addressed the possibility that skin lesions in CHILD syndrome primarily reflect cholesterol (pathway end-product) deficiency alone, but found no clinical improvement after 3 months of treatment with twice daily topical 10% cholesterol in hydrophilic ointment.
evidence.explanation: This sequential observation argues against cholesterol-alone efficacy in the two patients; no statin-only arm tested the necessity of supplementation.

evidence.snippet: Herein, we report a case of successful treatment of the cutaneous features of CHILD syndrome with compounded simvastatin and cholesterol gel and highlight the role of the compounding pharmacist in the care of patients with congenital ichthyosis.
evidence.explanation: An additional uncontrolled case report describes cutaneous benefit with compounded simvastatin/cholesterol gel.

treatments/0.description: Topical lovastatin or simvastatin combined with cholesterol has improved cutaneous lesions in uncontrolled reports. In the original two-patient study, 10% cholesterol alone produced no improvement over three months, followed by substantial improvement with 2% lovastatin/2% cholesterol. There was no statin-only arm, so this sequence does not establish that cholesterol supplementation is required. Later reports describe benefit from statin monotherapy. Skin improvement does not establish correction of congenital skeletal defects, and long-term comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

evidence.snippet: On the basis of the putative pathogenic role of both pathway-product deficiency of cholesterol and accumulation of toxic metabolic intermediates, we assessed the efficacy of combined therapy with lovastatin and cholesterol.
evidence.explanation: The authors state the dual treatment rationale as putative. The combined intervention does not isolate restoration of cholesterol from suppression of precursor formation.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: The cholesterol component supplies the pathway end product; tissue-specific target engagement was not isolated from the effects of the statin in the clinical report.

evidence.snippet: On the basis of the putative pathogenic role of both pathway-product deficiency of cholesterol and accumulation of toxic metabolic intermediates, we assessed the efficacy of combined therapy with lovastatin and cholesterol.
evidence.explanation: The authors state the dual treatment rationale as putative. The combined intervention does not isolate restoration of cholesterol from suppression of precursor formation.

treatments/0/targets/1.description: Upstream statin inhibition is intended to reduce precursor production; clinical response to the combination is consistent with this rationale but does not quantify precursor clearance.

evidence.explanation: The primary case used simvastatin monotherapy.

evidence.snippet: Decreased inflammation, skin thickening, and scaling were noted as early as 3 weeks. By 6 weeks, the treated skin largely and dramatically normalized with a discrete postinflammatory hypopigmentation remaining
evidence.explanation: Clinical results describe improvement by three weeks and near-normalization at six weeks.

evidence.snippet: No reoccurrence was observed after 10 months of maintenance topical treatment
evidence.explanation: Continued maintenance accompanied the reported sustained response.

treatments/1.description: Uncontrolled reports describe improvement with topical simvastatin without added cholesterol. In an infant treated with 2% ointment twice daily, improvement appeared by three weeks and the skin largely normalized by six weeks, with maintenance treatment over ten months. A later 5% report describes variable responses by site and recurrent lesions; it follows the previously reported p.Gly44Ser patient rather than adding an independent genotype case. Comparative efficacy and long-term safety are not established.

treatments/2.description: Off-label topical 2% ketoconazole has improved cutaneous lesions in individual reports. DLQI decreased from 3 to 1, with no apparent adverse effects during two and a half months of follow-up. This uncontrolled observation does not establish equivalence to statins or durable remission after stopping treatment.

Age-dependent selection in mouse liver and brain is a separate observation; human skin clone clearance has not been measured longitudinally. Mouse and canine lesion patterns differ from typical human lateralization. Paired spatial and allele-expression measurements could distinguish developmental lineage allocation from subsequent tissue-specific selection.

open_questions/1.rationale: Nsdhl mouse studies associate placental labyrinth abnormalities with prenatal death, but the timing varies by allele and the findings do not establish a universal human mechanism. Rodent and human placental X-inactivation differ. A report of recurrent male pregnancy losses identified maternal and fetal NSDHL c.790-6C>T, but classified it as a variant of uncertain significance, predicted a splice effect without functional confirmation, and tested only one lost conceptus. That report does not confirm NSDHL-mediated recurrent fetal lethality or the placental mechanism in humans.

evidence.snippet: We speculate that at least some cases of CHILD syndrome are allelic with CDPX2 caused by 3beta-hydroxysteroid-delta8,delta7-isomerase deficiency.
